title: The Untold Story of John
paragraphs: There are some men in Scripture who arrive like thunder.
Moses split seas. David killed giants. Paul shook empires.
A fisherman. A son. A brother. A young man with calloused hands smelling like saltwater and dead fish.
he became the disciple who leaned against the chest of God.
Most believers know fragments of his story.
They know him as “the disciple Jesus loved.” They know he wrote Revelation. They know him as the apostle of love.
But very few understand who John really was before grace transformed him.
Because the untold story of John is not the story of a naturally gentle man.
It is the story of a violent heart conquered by Jesus Christ.
And if God could transform John...
The first time we truly see John in Scripture, he is not soft.
In Mark 3:17, Jesus gives James and John a shocking nickname:
John was not originally known for compassion.
Most people never realize this because we only remember the elderly John writing lovingly about Christ decades later.
Luke 9 records one of the most revealing moments in John’s life.
“Lord, do You want us to command fire to come down from heaven and consume them?”
The Greek wording is terrifyingly forceful.
John was ready to burn human beings alive because they dishonored Christ.
Angry. Reactive. Harsh. Quick to condemn.
Calling wrath “discernment.” Calling bitterness “truth.” Calling cruelty “boldness.”
John understood religious rage before he understood divine love.
Some ancient manuscripts preserve a powerful longer reading from Luke 9:55:
“Ye know not what manner of spirit ye are of.”
Οὐκ οἴδατε οἵου πνεύματός ἐστε ὑμεῖς
“You do not know what spirit you belong to.”
That sentence should terrify every believer.
Because it means someone can defend Jesus publicly while operating from the wrong spirit internally.
But passion without surrender becomes destruction.
And maybe that is where you are right now.
But you are angry all the time.
but there is poison in your heart.
but secretly battle envy, lust, pride, resentment, addiction, hypocrisy, hidden compromise.
John did not become the apostle of love overnight.
He became that man by staying close to Jesus long enough for Jesus to kill the old version of him.
That is the part nobody talks about.
Jesus did not merely improve John.
There is a reason John later wrote:
The word used is not emotional affection.
A self-sacrificing, holy, covenantal love flowing from God Himself.
John wrote those words as an old man.
But those words were written by someone who once wanted to incinerate villages.
That is what makes the Gospel unbelievable.
Jesus does not just forgive sinners.
And perhaps nowhere is this seen more powerfully than at the cross.
The smell of iron and death filling the air.
The One John once believed would establish earthly triumph.
And yet John remained near Him.
“When Jesus therefore saw His mother, and the disciple standing by, whom He loved...”
Never underestimate the power of staying close to Jesus when your understanding collapses.
Peter denied Jesus. Thomas doubted Jesus. Judas betrayed Jesus.
the heart that once wanted to destroy enemies became the heart that wrote:
The Son of Thunder became the Apostle of Love.
Not because he attended enough services. Not because he learned religious language. Not because he perfected himself.
But because he stayed near Jesus.
And maybe it is your story too.
Because some of you reading this have become exhausted pretending.
You smile publicly while silently collapsing.
You worship outwardly while fighting darkness inwardly.
You know Bible verses but still cry at night.
You are terrified somebody will discover who you really are.
John was not loved because he was perfect.
He was loved while he was still being transformed.
And maybe that is why John described himself repeatedly as:
Because he never got over the fact that Jesus could love someone like him.
A thunderous man. A flawed man. An emotional man. A broken man.
some of you still have not accepted that either.
But not that He truly loves you.
You think your secret sin disqualified you. Your past ruined you. Your hypocrisy exposed you. Your addiction destroyed your future.
But John’s life screams another message.
Grace can rewrite people nobody expected God to use.
Years later, after persecution, suffering, exile, and immense loss, John would be banished to Patmos.
Most of his fellow apostles dead.
The Roman Empire attempting to silence Christianity.
Eyes like fire. Voice like many waters. Face shining like the sun.
And the same John who once called for fire from heaven collapsed like a dead man before the holiness of Jesus.
Because maturity in Christ does not make people arrogant.
The closer John came to Jesus...
the less impressive John became in his own eyes.
Some of you need to hear this today:
Jesus is not asking you to manufacture holiness by human strength.
He is asking you to remain near Him.
It means: remain, stay, continue, dwell.
Even through confusion. Even through failure. Even through fear. Even through grief.
And eventually the presence of Christ transformed the thunder inside him into holy love.
That is why this story matters.
Because modern Christianity often celebrates appearances more than transformation.
But Jesus is still changing people from the inside out.
Still healing. Still confronting. Still restoring. Still calling broken people closer.

Maybe you are reading this while battling pornography. Maybe you are drowning in anxiety. Maybe your marriage feels dead. Maybe you secretly hate yourself. Maybe you are exhausted by hidden sin. Maybe you are losing faith. Maybe you smile in church while bleeding internally.
John’s story proves that proximity to Jesus changes people over time.
Somebody else reading your honesty may realize they are not fighting alone.
The man who once wanted fire to destroy people became the man who taught the world how to love.
